summary.headline: Monte Carlo Q1 FY27 revenue rose 8% to INR149 crores, but a net loss of INR23 crores came from about INR130 crores of B2B sales returns pulled into the quarter.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR149 crores, up 8% YoY, with EBITDA loss of INR13 crores and net loss of INR23 crores. Management attributed the loss to front-loaded processing of B2B returns (about 65% of the full-period return volume recognised in Q1 versus 50% last year), which it says will even out over Q2 to Q4. Management guided to low double-digit revenue growth for FY27 (cut from an earlier 15-20% view, citing geopolitical tensions, inflation and monsoon risk), SSSG of about 10%, 40-45 new stores, and an EBITDA margin up to 100 bps lower than FY26's ~18%. Most Q&A focused on returns, the solar project, buyback requests and the low valuation.

segments.name: Cotton (basics/T-shirts)
segments.commentary: Volumes up 23% YoY per opening remarks (about 24% per analyst); management says cotton margin is about 100 bps better than winter wear and ~45% of sales, with a target to surpass winter sales in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Home textile
segments.commentary: Volumes up 42% YoY (about 40% per analyst); FY26 revenue about INR170 crores, FY27 guided to about INR215 crores (20-25% growth).

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Sales up 38% YoY in Q1; management calls it an emerging category under the lifestyle push.

segments.name: Online / digital
segments.commentary: Online sales up 15% YoY; own website is about 20% of online sales, with quick commerce (Blinkit, Swiggy, Zepto) partnerships. Direct-to-consumer (website plus ~145 company-owned EBOs) is about 3-4% of total sales per management.

segments.name: Solar (new vertical)
segments.commentary: About 50 MW DC project, INR147-150 crores investment, in Madhya Pradesh under a 25-year PPA via a wholly owned SPV; no capex spent so far; commissioning expected in 9-12 months.

guidance_outlook: Revenue: low double-digit growth for FY27 (management declined to quantify further); earlier view of 15-20% was cut because of geopolitical tensions, inflation and monsoon risk.
EBITDA margin: management said it could be up to 100 bps lower than FY26 (about 18%); may be flat or better if input costs ease over the next 3-4 months. Update promised at the Q2 call.
Same-store sales growth target about 10% for FY27 (FY26 was about 11%).
Store addition: 40-45 exclusive brand outlets in FY27, focused on west and south; franchisee ROI 3-4 years; company capex limited to about 10-15% of stores.
Price hikes: about 6-7% taken at winter trade show; another 8-10% planned for summer season.
Capex: about INR30 crores guided for FY28 (warehousing done, machine modernisation INR10-15 crores per year); no major manufacturing capex planned, incremental demand to be outsourced.
Advertising around 3% of sales for the full year; quarterly phasing can shift.
Returns target about 12-13% of sales, versus about 11% company-level return rate cited by management; the aim is 30-50 bps lower than last year.
capex_capacity: Woolen: 15-17 new machines added; cotton plants running at full capacity with no spare capacity, so incremental demand is to be outsourced to third-party vendors.
Returns refinishing capacity doubled (from 5,000 to 10,000 pieces per day) via added warehouse space and manpower.

Solar: about 50 MW DC, INR147-150 crores investment, land being aggregated; PPA signed with Madhya Pradesh government; billing expected from next financial year; management wants to commission and bill before new tenders. Plants are leased land (25-30 year leases), EPC-installed. Exit permitted only 1 year after commissioning.
Cash on books stated as INR305 crores (transcript reads 'INR30S crores'), not yet committed to solar; buyback is 'under Board discussion' with no decision announced.
demand_pricing: Q1 sales were hit by B2B returns (about INR130 crores; 1 lakh extra pieces returned vs last year). Management expects about 70,000 fewer pieces returned in Q2 than last year; combined Q1+Q2 return volume to rise 35,000-45,000 pieces, in line with dispatch growth.
Returns are 100% B2B (retailers), with management able to limit pickups; management says returns run ~11-12% company-wide vs 15-20% industry.
Order book supported growth, but management consciously cut production in view of geopolitical tensions and inflation.
Operating cost pressure from freight, packing and inputs; raw materials are pre-booked, so impact is limited, per management.
Management says ~20% organised share of Indian apparel vs 35-50% in developed markets, citing long-term runway.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue grow under 10% when cotton and home textile volumes rose about 20-40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher B2B returns (about INR80 crores more than last year, about INR130 crores in total) absorbed the revenue; returns were pulled forward because of added refinishing capacity. Returns are booked at cost, and the inventory is rebilled later.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the opening provision of about INR180 crores not netting the full Q1 returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said returns arrive across two financial years, so the INR180 crores provision covers the full year. Q1 consumes part of it, and the rest is spread over Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 guidance for revenue, SSSG and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Low double-digit revenue growth, about 10% SSSG, 40-45 stores, and EBITDA margin up to 100 bps lower than last year; management will update in the Q2 call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar project's contract structure and exit route?
qa_highlights.answer: Leased land on 25-30 year terms; 25-year PPA with the Madhya Pradesh government; run through a wholly owned SPV; exit allowed one year after commissioning, with buyers available at a cash-flow discount rate.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company consider a share buyback given the low P/E and the cash on books?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buyback is always under Board discussion, with no decision; a promoter (Diwakar/Gunit-raised) suggestion was noted, and management said 'by next quarter, you should see something'.

qa_highlights.question: Are there exports or FTA benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: No exports at present beyond small Middle East online sales under own brand; the company is an asset-light retailer that outsources most production, so FTA benefits are not expected.
